## Dynamical Systems


a *phase space* $x \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$, $n$ the degrees of freedom
$$\frac{d x}{dt} := \dot{x} = f(x)$$




---

### autonomous Hamiltonian systems

$x=(p,q) \in \mathbb{R}^{2d}$, and $p,q \in \mathbb{R}^d$

$$\begin{pmatrix}\dot{p} \\ \dot{q} \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}-\frac{\partial H(x)}{\partial q} \\  \frac{\partial H(x)}{\partial p} \end{pmatrix}$$

---

### Hamiltonian systems {data-transition="slide"}



$x=(p,q) \in \mathbb{R}^{2d}$, and $p,q \in \mathbb{R}^d$


$$f(x)= \begin{pmatrix}0 & -\mathbb{1} \\ \mathbb{1} & 0\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} \tfrac{\partial H(x)}{\partial p} \\ \tfrac{\partial H(x)}{\partial q}\end{pmatrix}$$

---

### Hamiltonian systems {data-transition="slide"}

$x=(p,q) \in \mathbb{R}^{2d}$, and $p,q \in \mathbb{R}^d$


$$f(x)= S \frac{\partial H(x)}{\partial x}$$



$S= \begin{pmatrix}0 & -\mathbb{1} \\ \mathbb{1} & 0\end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} \Rightarrow$ **symplectic geometry**: conservation of phase–space volume!

---

### Periodic trajectories

A trajectory is $\Phi(t,x)$ solves $\dot{x}=f(x)$: $\Phi(T,x)=x$
